page: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the ESv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 32.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between memory capacity and processing throughput. Single-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1409.58 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1225.0, both falling into the average tier. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are generally weak. The multi-core stress-ng score is 3699.56, and large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is limited to 24.02 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks also reflect these limitations, with a Passmark CPU encryption score of 1713.87 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 23.75 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance allocates a disproportionately large memory footprint relative to its compute resources. This makes it a specialized choice for workloads that require substantial RAM but have low parallel processing demands. It is suited for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads such as caching layers, small to medium relational databases with large working sets, and basic data processing tasks that fit entirely within memory but do not require high multi-threaded CPU throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-4s_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv4 family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores) and 128.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high 32.0 GB per vCPU memory ratio. The server features no local storage or GPUs but supports Premium Storage. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1225.0, but weak multi-core and memory bandwidth performance, as evidenced by a multi-core stress-ng score of 3699.56 and uncached read bandwidth of 24.02 GB/sec. This hardware profile is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound applications with low CPU scaling requirements. It is best suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory caching, database hosting, and lightweight data processing.
